title: A comparison of citation-based clustering and topic modeling for science mapping
task: Comparing LDA topics with citation-based clusters for mapping a research field
problem: Topic modelling and citation-based clustering are both used for science maps, but how their results relate is poorly understood.
architecture: LDA (Gensim) on titles and abstracts, topics visualised with PCA and labelled with expert input; citation-based clustering from the CWTS hierarchical classification (Waltman-van Eck, Leiden algorithm), 142 micro-level clusters with at least 10% cardiovascular publications, visualised with VOSviewer; cluster-to-topic and topic-to-cluster mappings.
metrics: document overlap between topics and clusters (mapping shares)
key_results: Overlap between topics and clusters is generally weak; only in a few cases do more than one-third of a topic's documents fall in one cluster or vice versa.
Topic modelling captures societal-need themes (risk factors, guidelines) but mixes disease terms; citation clustering separates diseases and micro-communities.
strengths: Large-scale, systematic comparison showing the two maps answer different questions.

limitations.text: Single field (cardiovascular research) and a single topic model (LDA).
No ground truth; highly similar LDA topics complicate interpretation.
